title: West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville targeting return from calf injury vs. Aston Villa
content:
West Ham United winger Crysencio Summerville is hopeful he will return to action against Aston Villa on March 22.

The 24-year-old sustained a calf injury in the FA Cup fifth-round penalty shootout victory against Brentford. Summerville picked up the knock in the second half of extra-time, but played the remainder of the game because head coach Nuno Espirito Santo had made all of his substitutions.

The attacker, who will miss his side’s upcoming Premier League home game against Manchester City, had an initial scan on Tuesday and will be assessed further this week.

Summerville has been a key performer since January, having registered seven goals and one assist across his last 13 games. Sources briefed on the situation, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, say Summerville is determined to return to action to help West Ham’s push for top-flight survival and to earn international recognition with the Netherlands.

Summerville, who has represented the Netherlands’ youth teams from under-16 to under-21 level, is in strong contention to earn his first senior call-up ahead of friendlies against Norway and Ecuador at the end of March.

Ruud van Nistelrooy, the assistant coach for the Netherlands’ national team, attended West Ham’s goalless draw against Bournemouth earlier this month, while head coach Ronald Koeman admitted the winger is on his radar.

“Our biggest competition is often in midfield and defence, but in attack, it’s a bit less,” Koeman told ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie. “He plays in the Premier League and is important there at West Ham United. He can play on the right and the left. We’re looking closely at that.”

In January 2025, Summerville injured his hamstring in an FA Cup game against Aston Villa and was sidelined for seven months. It was the longest injury layoff of his career. He made his return in the 3-0 away victory against Nottingham Forest, then managed by Nuno, on August 31.

Despite Summerville’s absence, West Ham will hope to maintain their good run of form against title chasers Manchester City. Nuno’s side have lost only two of their last 11 games in all competitions. Although West Ham remain in the relegation zone, level on points with Forest, victory could see them climb out for the first time since November.

Fellow relegation contenders Forest and Tottenham Hotspur face Fulham and Liverpool respectively this Sunday.

The winger is a key attacking outlet on the left side of West Ham’s attack. The only obvious replacement is Adama Traore, who joined in January on a permanent transfer from Fulham.

The 30-year-old, who Nuno recently banned from lifting weights at the club’s training ground, started on the left flank in a 4-3-3 formation against Brentford. He was fouled in the penalty area by full-back Michael Kayode, which club captain Jarrod Bowen converted. Traore was substituted at half-time for Summerville.

The former Wolverhampton Wanderers winger is yet to start a league game for West Ham. He has made cameo appearances from the bench against Fulham, Liverpool, Manchester United, Burnley and Chelsea.

“I think the squad has accepted him really well,” Nuno told a press conference before the 1-0 win over London rivals Fulham. “He has brought new energy to us. We’ve been trying every day to help him. But of course ahead of him he has two players at the top of their game in Bowen and Summerville. Traore’s patient enough to realise his chance will come.”

That could be sooner than Nuno expected.
